pull_requests.body:
Bumps [@neondatabase/serverless](https://github.com/neondatabase/serverless) from 1.1.0 to 1.2.0.
Changelog

Sourced from @​neondatabase/serverless's changelog.

1.2.0 (2026-10-01)

  • Options to the neon(...) HTTP-client creation function, and to the transaction and query functions, now support individual connection parameters: user (or username), password, host (or hostname), port, database and connectionString.

    These can be strings (or number, for port) or sync or async functions to be resolved on every query. They can supplement, override parts of, or fully replace the first-argument connection string.

    So this still works:

    • const sql = neon(DATABASE_URL)

    But, for example, these now work too:

    • const sql = neon(DATABASE_URL_NO_PASSWORD, { password: () => getPasswordAsync() })
    • const sql = neon({ user, password, host, database })
    • const sql = neon({ connectionString: () => getConnectionString() })

  • Client and Pool now support a sync or async function as the password connection parameter when pipelineConnect is enabled (this previously caused an error). And parseIntoClientConfig from pg-connection-string is exported at top-level to make it easy to use a password function alongside a connection string:

    import { Pool, parseIntoClientConfig } from '@neondatabase/serverless';

    const pool = new Pool({
    
...parseIntoClientConfig(process.env.DATABASE_URL),
    
password: () => getDatabaseAuthToken('argument'),
    
});

  • A few other minor fixes.

  • The package is no longer published to JSR. Please update any jsr references to npm:@neondatabase/serverless.

4.0.114

pull_requests.body:
Bumps [tailwindcss](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/tailwindcss/tree/HEAD/packages/tailwindcss) from 4.3.3 to 4.3.5.
Release notes

Sourced from tailwindcss's releases.

v4.3.5

Fixed

  • Canonicalization: improve performance in projects with many functional variant values (e.g. a matchVariant plugin with thousands of values) (#20663)
  • Don't crash or create a fallback with the wrong color for a color-mix(…) without a color interpolation method (e.g. color-mix(var(--color-red-500)) or color-mix(currentcolor 50%, transparent)) (#20658, #20666)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi loads instead of hanging forever (e.g. with NAPI_RS_FORCE_WASI=error or in WebContainers) (#20667)
  • Remove as: '*.css' from the @tailwindcss/turbopack setup in its README, because it breaks CSS modules (#20660)
  • Ignore <!-- and --> between top-level rules in CSS instead of throwing or swallowing the next rule (e.g. a { color: red } --> b { color: blue }) (#20665)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi detects changed and new source files after the first scan (e.g. in WebContainers) (#20487)
  • Prevent type errors with skipLibCheck: false caused by imports of unshipped modules in the @tailwindcss/node type declarations (#20632)

v4.3.4

Added

  • Add @tailwindcss/turbopack, a Turbopack loader for using Tailwind CSS with Next.js (#20367)

Fixed

  • Ensure watch mode detects changes to symlinked @source files whose real paths aren't otherwise scanned (#20356)
  • Ensure variants using @scope wrap generated utilities instead of nesting inside them (#20369)
  • Ensure nested @scope rules preserve their scoping semantics when flattened (#20369)
  • Preserve declarations directly inside @scope by wrapping them in :where(:scope) (#20369)
  • Ensure generated utilities include a space in empty var() fallbacks (e.g. var(--tw-blur,) → var(--tw-blur, )) (#20373)
  • Canonicalization: convert arbitrary breakpoint and container query variants to named equivalents (e.g. max-[64rem]:flex → max-lg:flex) (#20380)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from crashing on every edit under Vite's experimental bundledDev mode (#20379)
  • Ensure @tailwindcss/oxide falls back to WASM on platforms without native bindings (@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi now installs on all platforms, but only loads when no native binding is available) (#20383)
  • Extract class candidates from Ruby %w and %W literals using angle brackets or custom delimiters (e.g. %w<flex>, %w|flex|), including in Slim and Haml templates (#20387)
  • Preserve whitespace in --default(…) values in functional @utility definitions (e.g. --default(box alphabetic) no longer becomes boxalphabetic) (#20392)
  • Ensure automatic source detection respects negation-based .gitignore files (e.g. /* followed by !/… patterns) (#20397)
  • Ensure root theme('…') namespace lookups in JavaScript plugins and config files return the full namespace object instead of the value of its DEFAULT key (#20399)
  • Skip ignored directories when generating watch globs instead of walking their contents on every rebuild (#20408)
  • Drop invalid UTF-8 candidates during class detection (#20389)
  • Prevent @tailwindcss/vite from forcing full-page reloads for scanned files that Vite does not handle as modules (e.g. .php files) (#20414)
  • Canonicalization: don't merge utilities that reference different theme variables set to CSS-wide keywords like unset (#20417)
  • Don't generate utilities when a modifier is used that would otherwise be silently ignored (e.g. rounded-sm/[5], shadow-sm/foo, stroke-2/50) (#20419)
  • Preserve and, or, and not inside selectors in supports-[…] variants (e.g. supports-[selector(a:not(.foo))]:flex) (#20420)
  • Don't warn about Angular's ::ng-deep and :host-context() when optimizing CSS (#20434)
  • Don't generate CSS for candidates containing an empty additional modifier (e.g. bg-red-500/50/ and group-hover/foo//bar:flex) (#20466)
  • Ensure min-*, max-*, and container query variants with decimal values are sorted numerically (e.g. min-[40.25rem] before min-[40.5rem]) (#20512)
  • Ensure CSS comments ending with \*/ are closed correctly instead of swallowing the CSS that follows (e.g. /* C:\temp\*/) (#20508)
  • Improve style invalidation performance of group-* and peer-* variants (#20513)
  • Ensure cached compilers release their loadModule and loadStylesheet callbacks after compilation (#20531)
  • Canonicalization: preserve & when moving a pseudo-element into * or ** (e.g. [&_::before]:flex → **:[&::before]:flex) (#20550)
  • Ensure the Set.prototype.intersection polyfill in canonicalizeCandidates(…) returns the intersection instead of the first set on Node.js < 22 (#20562)
  • Canonicalization: ensure inline theme(…) alphas with more than 2 decimals migrate to a percentage modifier with the same opacity (e.g. theme(colors.red.500/.12345) → text-red-500/[12.345%], not text-red-500/[12.345]) (#20563)
  • Canonicalization: preserve inline theme(…) alphas as an arbitrary percentage when a custom --opacity-* theme value would change the opacity (e.g. theme(colors.red.500/50%) → text-red-500/[50%] with --opacity-50: 10%) (#20563)
  • Ensure the @property fallback isn't applied in Safari versions that no longer support margin-trim: inline (#20569)
  • Treat viewport units like dvmin and svi and font-relative units like cap and rex as lengths in arbitrary values (e.g. text-[10dvmin] generates font-size instead of color) (#20516)
  • Write plugin logs to stderr in tailwindcss canonicalize so they don't end up in the results on stdout (#20561)
  • Extract class shorthands on later lines when Pug text, comments, or quoted attribute values contain unbalanced brackets, or a quote that doesn't start a string (e.g. input(pattern=/"/.source)) (#20547, #20572)

Bumps [github/codeql-action/analyze](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) from 5895b2c9be147bc7f1c75ce72c5cb577febb1907 to 33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066.
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/analyze's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.3 - 04 Nov 2026

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

4.39.2 - 03 Nov 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129
